links.targetTitle: Penalties are graduated for Aligned Delegates but mandatory

title: No adjudication process exists for misalignment by Ecosystem Actors or other governance participants
content:
A.1.7.6 grants the Core Facilitator "broad discretion in addressing situations where an Alignment Conserver, **Ecosystem Actor or other relevant governance participant's** actions are misaligned" — but the process it cites, A.1.5.9, is titled and scoped to Alignment Conserver adjudication.

NR-17 names the gap precisely: "Currently, the Atlas specifies an adjudication process for Alignment Conserver misalignment or breach of operational security. Research is needed to consider a process by which Facilitators investigate and adjudicate suspected misalignment on the part of Ecosystem Actors or other governance participants."

This is corroborated from an unexpected direction. The worked Scenario at A.1.5.5.0.4.1.1.2, where an Aligned Delegate takes a second role as an on-call developer for an Ecosystem Actor, ends with the flat admission: "No specific logic exists as yet for the adjudication of misalignment on the part of an Ecosystem Actor team member." The AD is derecognized; the EA side of the same arrangement has no process at all. The Variation makes it starker — when both the EA and the entity stonewall the investigation, the guidance can only note that this "is a strong indication of malign intent on the part of Entity **and the EA**" while still acting solely against the AD.

The asymmetry is consequential given A.1.8.1's grant: Active and Incubating Ecosystem Actors "are the only type of actor that is permitted to do work that isn't strictly defined in, and bounded by, the Atlas." The population with the widest discretion is the one without a defined accountability process, while the population with the narrowest discretion — ACs — carries mandatory derecognition on a 51% finding.

The practical result is that the Atlas's enforcement power falls hardest on its own guardians and lightest on its contractors, which is the opposite of what the discretion each holds would suggest.
description: NR-17 records that the Atlas defines adjudication only for Alignment Conservers, even though A.1.7.6 already empowers the Core Facilitator to address Ecosystem Actor misalignment.
